title: SG 94 17 17 sweet potato (UPL Sp 13): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: SG 94 17 17 sweet potato: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: SG 94 17 17 sweet potato is a sweet potato variety. About 120 days to harvest, 13 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: SG 94 17 17 is a registered sweet potato variety, also sold or known as UPL Sp 13 or NSIC Sp 23. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Sp 23. It comes from IPB UPLB. It takes about 120 days from planting to harvest, with 13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

SG 94 17 17 sweet potato takes about 120 days from planting to harvest. That is 5.5 days longer than the average of the 26 sweet potato varieties with a day count, 114.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 13 t/ha trails the average of its group, 15.15. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 120 days, 105 to 120 days (DA Caraga).

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit sweet potato fields most often: [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have yellow flesh and purple skin. Dry matter is 33 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 25.9 percent.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 13 t/ha in registry trials, DA Caraga guide cites about 16 t/ha.
**Fruit:** Purple skin, yellow flesh, elliptical roots, dry matter 33 percent, flour 25.9 percent.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: kept by Central Luzon growers after a participatory trial of 24 varieties, and one of three varieties in DA Caraga's kamote guide. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant SG 94 17 17 sweet potato

The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Pick by use and market: yellow or orange flesh for snacks and fries, purple for processing, white for boiling. Weevils are the main enemy, so plant clean cuttings and harvest on time.

items.q: Is UPL Sp 13 the same as SG 94 17 17?
items.a: Yes. UPL Sp 13 is another name for SG 94 17 17, registered as NSIC 2000 Sp 23. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 120 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of SG 94 17 17?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
